'''Brandon Datrelle Goodwin''' (born October 2, 1995) is an American-born naturalized Qatari professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Shanghai Sharks]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[UCF Knights men's basketball|UCF Knights]] and the [[Florida Gulf Coast Eagles men's basketball|Florida Gulf Coast Eagles]], being named the 2018 [[ASUN Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|ASUN Conference Player of the Year]] with the latter.

==College career==
Goodwin, a 6'0" [[point guard]], committed to [[UCF Knights men's basketball|UCF]] from [[Norcross High School]]. He played for the Knights in the [[2013–14 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2013–14]] and [[2014–15 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2014–15]] seasons. He left UCF after being caught taking (though later returning) a bike on campus the summer after his freshman year.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Forgrave|first1=Reid|title=FGCU's Brandon Goodwin trades troubled past for bright future at Dunk City|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/fgcus-brandon-goodwin-trades-troubled-past-for-bright-future-at-dunk-city/|access-date=February 25, 2018|work=[[CBSSports.com]]|date=November 17, 2017|archive-date=February 26, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180226092156/https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/fgcus-brandon-goodwin-trades-troubled-past-for-bright-future-at-dunk-city/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Soffian|first1=Seth|title=Alpha dog: Brandon Goodwin the star FGCU almost didn't have|url=https://www.news-press.com/story/sports/college/fgcu/2017/02/11/alpha-dog-brandon-goodwin-star-fgcu-almost-didnt-have/97806436/|access-date=February 25, 2018|work=[[The News-Press]]|date=February 14, 2017|archive-date=October 14, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211014232905/https://www.news-press.com/story/sports/college/fgcu/2017/02/11/alpha-dog-brandon-goodwin-star-fgcu-almost-didnt-have/97806436/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Goodwin landed at [[Florida Gulf Coast Eagles men's basketball|Florida Gulf Coast]] (FGCU) after leaving UCF. After sitting out a season as a transfer, he averaged 18.5 points, 4.5 rebounds and 4.1 assists per game and was named [[ASUN Conference]] Newcomer of the Year.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Hays|first1=Chris|title=UCF transfer Brandon Goodwin returns to Orlando with Florida Gulf Coast|url=http://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/college/marchmadness/os-sp-fgcu-brandon-goodwin-0316-story.html|access-date=February 25, 2018|work=[[Orlando Sentinel]]|date=March 15, 2017|archive-date=February 26, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180226092134/http://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/college/marchmadness/os-sp-fgcu-brandon-goodwin-0316-story.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He then led the Eagles to an NCAA Tournament berth after earning [[Atlantic Sun men's basketball tournament|Atlantic Sun tournament]] MVP honors.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Caldwell|first1=Dana|title=Time of his life: Interesting journey of FGCU's Goodwin|url=https://www.news-press.com/story/sports/college/fgcu/2017/03/11/time-life-interesting-journey-fgcus-goodwin/99078110/|access-date=February 25, 2018|work=[[The News-Press]]|date=March 11, 2017|archive-date=October 14, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211014232905/https://www.news-press.com/story/sports/college/fgcu/2017/03/11/time-life-interesting-journey-fgcus-goodwin/99078110/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Following his junior season, Goodwin declared for the [[2017 NBA draft]] without signing with an agent, ultimately deciding to return to FGCU for his senior year.<ref>{{cite news|title=College basketball: FGCU's Brandon Goodwin takes name out of NBA Draft|url=https://www.naplesnews.com/story/sports/college/fgcu/2017/05/24/college-basketball-fgcus-brandon-goodwin-takes-name-out-nba-draft/343699001/|access-date=February 25, 2018|work=[[Naples Daily News]]|date=May 24, 2017|archive-date=January 11, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180111072858/http://www.naplesnews.com/story/sports/college/fgcu/2017/05/24/college-basketball-fgcus-brandon-goodwin-takes-name-out-nba-draft/343699001/|url-status=live}}</ref>

In his senior year, Goodwin led the Eagles to a regular season Atlantic Sun championship and was named first-team All-Atlantic Sun and the Atlantic Sun Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://asunsports.org/sports/mbkb/2017-18/releases/20180225h77kuh |title=FGCU's Goodwin grabs @ASUNMBB top honor; postseason awards announced |publisher=Atlantic Sun Conference |date=February 25, 2018 |access-date=February 25, 2018}}</ref> He averaged 18.6 points, 5.5 rebounds, 4.8 assists and 1.4 steals per game as a senior.<ref>{{cite news |title=Grizzlies' Brandon Goodwin: Gets camp deal from Grizzlies |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/grizzlies-brandon-goodwin-gets-camp-deal-from-grizzlies/ |access-date=September 4, 2018 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=September 4, 2018 |archive-date=September 5, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180905023158/https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/grizzlies-brandon-goodwin-gets-camp-deal-from-grizzlies/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Memphis Hustle (2018)===
After going undrafted in the [[2018 NBA draft]], Goodwin signed with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] for the [[2018 NBA Summer League]]. On September 4, he joined the Grizzlies for training camp.<ref>{{cite web |title=Grizzlies sign Brandon Goodwin |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-brandon-goodwin-180904 |website=NBA.com |access-date=September 4, 2018 |date=September 4, 2018 |archive-date=September 28, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200928213217/https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-brandon-goodwin-180904 |url-status=live }}</ref> He was waived on October 13, as one of the final roster cuts before opening night.<ref>{{cite web |title=Memphis Grizzlies finalize 2018-19 regular season roster |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-finalize-2018-19-regular-season-roster-181013 |website=NBA.com |access-date=October 14, 2018 |date=October 13, 2018 |archive-date=October 14, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181014010422/https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-finalize-2018-19-regular-season-roster-181013 |url-status=live }}</ref> Goodwin was subsequently added to the roster of the Grizzlies' [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Memphis Hustle]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Memphis Hustle announce 2018-19 Training Camp Roster|url=https://memphis.gleague.nba.com/news/memphis-hustle-announce-2018-19-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 20, 2018|access-date=October 25, 2018|archive-date=October 26, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181026025520/https://memphis.gleague.nba.com/news/memphis-hustle-announce-2018-19-training-camp-roster/|url-status=live}}</ref> In nine appearances with the Hustle, Goodwin averaged 23.4 points, 5.3 rebounds and 4 assists per game.

===Denver Nuggets (2018–2019)===
On November 29, 2018, Goodwin was signed by the [[Denver Nuggets]]. The Nuggets were granted an injury hardship relief exception from the NBA, allowing them to add Goodwin to their otherwise full roster.<ref>{{cite web|title=Denver Nuggets Sign Brandon Goodwin|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/denver-nuggets-sign-brandon-goodwin-112918|website=NBA.com|date=November 29, 2018|access-date=November 29, 2018|archive-date=October 14, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211014232907/https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/denver-nuggets-sign-brandon-goodwin-112918-2|url-status=live}}</ref> He was waived on December 10, without appearing in any games.<ref>{{cite web|title=Denver Nuggets Sign Nick Young, Waive Brandon Goodwin|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-nick-young-waive-goodwin-121018-2|website=NBA.com|date=December 10, 2018|access-date=December 10, 2018|archive-date=November 29, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201129081427/https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-nick-young-waive-goodwin-121018-2|url-status=live}}</ref>

On December 13, 2018, the [[Memphis Hustle]] announced that Goodwin had returned to their team.<ref>{{cite news|first=Geoff|last=Langham|title=Brandon Goodwin returns to Memphis Hustle|url=https://memphis.gleague.nba.com/news/brandon-goodwin-returns-to-memphis-hustle|date=December 13, 2018|work=NBA.com|access-date=December 13, 2018|archive-date=December 15, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181215175649/https://memphis.gleague.nba.com/news/brandon-goodwin-returns-to-memphis-hustle/|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later the Nuggets re-signed Goodwin to a [[two-way contract]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Denver Nuggets Sign Brandon Goodwin, Waive DeVaughn Akoon-Purcell|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-goodwin-waive-akoon-purcell-121618-3|website=NBA.com|date=December 16, 2018|access-date=December 17, 2018|archive-date=December 17, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181217154742/https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-goodwin-waive-akoon-purcell-121618-3|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Atlanta Hawks (2019–2021)===
[[File:Brandon Goodwin crop.jpg|thumb|left|Goodwin with the Hawks in 2020]]
On August 6, 2019, Goodwin signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Hawks Sign Brandon Goodwin To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-sign-brandon-goodwin-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|access-date=August 6, 2019|date=August 6, 2019|archive-date=August 7, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190807124709/https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-sign-brandon-goodwin-two-way-contract|url-status=live}}</ref> On February 12, 2020, the [[Atlanta Hawks]] announced that they had re-signed Goodwin to a multi-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Brandon Goodwin to Multi-Year Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/features/atlanta-hawks-sign-brandon-goodwin-multi-year-contract|date=February 12, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 12, 2020|archive-date=February 13, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200213013547/https://www.nba.com/hawks/features/atlanta-hawks-sign-brandon-goodwin-multi-year-contract|url-status=live}}</ref> Goodwin missed the [[2021 NBA playoffs]] due to a respiratory condition. On October 3, 2021, with his season having ended early, Goodwin reported severe fatigue coupled with extreme back pain, and a formal diagnosis of blood clots followed. Goodwin initially blamed a COVID vaccination for his condition but later indicated he wasn't sure.<ref>{{cite news |last=Kertscher |first=Tom |date=October 22, 2001 |title=How rare are blood clots associated with the COVID-19 vaccine? |url=https://www.statesman.com/story/news/politics/2021/10/22/how-rare-blood-clots-associated-covid-19-vaccine/6118340001/ |work=[[PolitiFact]] |via=[[Austin American-Statesman]] |access-date=August 11, 2023 |quote=Goodwin, who is not currently with an NBA team, said himself in an October video that he blamed the vaccine "a thousand percent" for clots that cut short his 2020-21 season with the Hawks. He seemed to walk back his claim when he later tweeted: "I got sick. Maybe it was the vaccine maybe it was covid (i don't know) I'm not a expert."}}</ref>

===Westchester Knicks (2021)===
On October 14, Goodwin was signed by the [[New York Knicks]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Knicks Sign Brandon Goodwin|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-sign-brandon-goodwin|website=NBA.com|date=October 14, 2021|access-date=October 16, 2021}}</ref> who waived him the next day.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=NY_KnicksPR|number=1449128732967456778|title=Knicks waive Brandon Goodwin.|user=NY_KnicksPR|date=October 15, 2021|access-date=October 16, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211016212111/https://twitter.com/NY_KnicksPR/status/1449128732967456778|archive-date=October 16, 2021|url-status=live}}</ref> In October 2021, he joined the [[Westchester Knicks]] as an affiliate player.<ref>{{cite web |title=Westchester Knicks Announce Training Camp Roster |url=https://westchester.gleague.nba.com/news/westchester-knicks-announce-training-camp-roster/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 1, 2021 |date=October 25, 2021}}</ref> He averaged 15.3 points, 5.1 rebounds, 7.0 assists and 1.9 steals per game.<ref name="cavs" />

===Cleveland Cavaliers (2021–2022)===
On December 31, 2021, Goodwin signed a 10-day contract with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] via the hardship exemption.<ref name="cavs">{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Sign Brandon Goodwin|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/goodwin-signing-211231|website=NBA.com|date=December 31, 2021|access-date=December 31, 2021}}</ref> On January 9, 2022, his deal was converted to a two-way contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cavaliers Convert Brandon Goodwin to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/goodwin-signing-220109|website=NBA.com|date=January 9, 2022|access-date=January 9, 2022|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220109235536/https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/goodwin-signing-220109|archive-date=January 9, 2022}}</ref>

===Return to Westchester (2023–2024)===
On October 19, 2023, Goodwin signed with the [[New York Knicks]],<ref>{{cite tweet|author=NY_KnicksPR|title=Knicks sign Mamadi Diakite and Brandon Goodwin|number=1715114425311490426|user=NY_KnicksPR|date=October 19, 2023|access-date=October 20, 2023}}</ref> but was waived two days later.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=NY_KnicksPR|title=Knicks waive Mamadi Diakite, Brandon Goodwin, Isaiah Roby and Duane Washington Jr.|number=1715832489313182178|user=NY_KnicksPR|date=October 21, 2023|access-date=October 22, 2023}}</ref> On November 9, 2023, Goodwin was named to the opening night roster for the [[Westchester Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Westchester Knicks Announce 2023-24 Official Roster|url=https://westchester.gleague.nba.com/news/westchester-knicks-announce-2023-24-official-roster|website=NBA.com|date=November 9, 2023|access-date=December 3, 2023}}</ref> On March 27, 2024, he reached a buyout with Westchester.<ref>{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Westchester Knicks Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Westchester-Knicks/40/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=March 28, 2024}}</ref>

===Cangrejeros de Santurce (2024)===
On March 5, 2024, Goodwin signed with the [[Cangrejeros de Santurce (basketball)|Cangrejeros de Santurce]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Cangrejeros anuncian a su segundo refuerzo para la temporada del BSN|url=https://www.metro.pr/deportes/2024/03/05/cangrejeros-anuncian-a-su-segundo-refuerzo-para-la-temporada-del-bsn/|website=Metro.pr|date=March 5, 2024|access-date=March 5, 2024|language=Spanish}}</ref>

===Gigantes de Carolina (2024)===
On April 19, 2024, Goodwin was acquired by the [[Gigantes de Carolina (men's basketball)|Gigantes de Carolina]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] after being let go by Santurce.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=La Guerra del BSN|title=#BSNPR {{¡}} ÚLTIMA HORA: El armador Brandon Goodwin es el nuevo refuerzo de los Gigantes de Carolina tras ser dejado en libertad por los Cangrejeros de Santurce. Carolina y Santurce culminan intercambiando refuerzos tras la llegada de Quinn Cook a los Cangrejeros. Goodwin viene de promediar 13.2 PPJ, 5.2 RPJ y 6.2 APJ con los Cangrejeros en esta temporada 2024.|number=1781413155941290063|user=LaGuerraBSN|date=April 19, 2024|access-date=April 20, 2024|language=Spanish}}</ref>
